title: Exponential families
dek: If the density is exp{(T(y)ᵀη − A(η))/φ + c(y,φ)}, then mean, variance, and the score are derivatives of A. That is why GLMs feel inevitable.
story: An exponential family is a sampling model whose log-density is linear in a finite sufficient statistic T(y). Once you write f(y | η) = h(y) exp{T(y)ᵀη − A(η)}, the whole dance of MLEs, Fisher information, and GLMs is derivatives of the log-partition A.

Bernoulli, Poisson, Gaussian with known variance, gamma, and multinomial all sit in this class (or a dispersion extension). The canonical parameter η is not always the mean: for Bernoulli, η = logit(π); for Poisson, η = log λ. That is why those links are called canonical.

Sufficiency is the practical punchline: the MLE depends on the data only through T(y). For iid Bernoulli, T = ∑ yᵢ. For iid Gaussian mean, T = ∑ yᵢ. If your “model” needs the whole list of residuals as a sufficient statistic, you have left the exponential family — not a crime, but you should know you left.
deepTitle: Mean, variance, and the GLM hook
deep: Natural-form density (scalar, for a lab notebook): f(y | θ, φ) = exp{(yθ − b(θ))/a(φ) + c(y,φ)}. Then E[Y] = b′(θ) and Var(Y) = b″(θ) a(φ). Fisher information for θ in one observation is b″(θ)/a(φ). The score (y − μ)/ (φ V(μ) g′(μ)) in a GLM is this derivative in costume.

Canonical link: set the linear predictor equal to the natural parameter, g(μ) = θ(μ). Logit is canonical for Bernoulli because θ = log(π/(1−π)). Log is canonical for Poisson because θ = log λ. Non-canonical links (probit, complementary log-log, identity-for-Poisson) are allowed; IRLS still works; interpretation and small-sample behaviour change.

Dispersion φ is known in strict Bernoulli/Poisson (φ = 1) and estimated in Gaussian and gamma. Quasi-likelihood keeps the mean–variance map V(μ) without committing to a full exponential-family density — the estimating equation is the same, the likelihood ratio is not.

In TB WGS–DST, a Bernoulli likelihood for a binary catalogue call is an exponential family. A finite-mixture of resistant and susceptible subpopulations is not a one-parameter exponential family in the mixture weight; the sufficient statistic is no longer a single count, and boundary issues appear.

formulas.label: One-parameter exponential family
formulas.expression: f(y | θ, φ) = exp{(yθ − b(θ))/a(φ) + c(y, φ)}

formulas.label: Canonical examples
formulas.expression: Bernoulli: θ = logit(π);   Poisson: θ = log λ;   N(μ,σ²): θ = μ/σ²
formulas.note: The GLM canonical link is the map μ ↦ θ(μ).

example.title: Poisson as an exponential family
example.setup: Colony counts Y ~ Poisson(λ) on a plate with exposure t already absorbed into λ. Write the density in exponential form and read off μ, V(μ), and the MLE from n iid plates.

steps.title: Rewrite the pmf
steps.body: P(Y=y) = e^{−λ} λ^y / y! = exp{y log λ − λ − log(y!)}. So θ = log λ, b(θ) = e^θ, a(φ) = 1, T(y) = y.

steps.title: Mean and variance
steps.body: b′(θ) = e^θ = λ, b″(θ) = e^θ = λ. Mean equals variance. That is the Poisson marriage a GLM will impose unless you move to quasi-Poisson or negative binomial.

steps.title: iid MLE
steps.body: ℓ(λ) = (∑ yᵢ) log λ − nλ. Score ∑ yᵢ/λ − n = 0 ⇒ λ̂ = ȳ. Sufficiency made the list of counts disappear except as a sum.

example.takeaway: If you can see T(y) and A(η), you already know the mean, the variance, and usually the MLE.

check.prompt: The canonical link for a Bernoulli likelihood is logit because:
choices: Logit is the only link that gives odds ratios
The natural parameter of the Bernoulli exponential family is log(π/(1−π))
check.answer: The natural parameter of the Bernoulli exponential family is log(π/(1−π))
check.why: Canonical means η = θ(μ). For Bernoulli that map is logit. Odds ratios are a consequence, not the definition. Probit is a perfectly legal non-canonical GLM.

whyWrong.Logit is the only link that gives odds r: Odds ratios come from a logit linear predictor, which is the canonical choice, but that is interpretation after the fact.
whyWrong.Probit is not a GLM: Probit is a Bernoulli GLM with a different link.

check.prompt: iid Poisson, n = 5, counts 0,1,3,2,4. What is the MLE of λ, and what sufficient statistic produced it?
check.why: In the Poisson exponential family T = ∑ yᵢ = 10, λ̂ = T/n = 2. The maximum observation is not sufficient.

whyWrong.λ̂ = 4, from max yᵢ: The max is not the sufficient statistic.
whyWrong.λ̂ = 0, from the zero count: One zero does not set the mean to 0.
whyWrong.λ̂ = 5, from n: n is the sample size, not the mean.

check.prompt: On the constellation plate, why is “mixture: not 1-p expfam” listed among the families?
check.figureHint: Terms include Bernoulli/logit and a mixture warning.
choices: Because mixtures are the canonical link for Poisson
To mark that a finite mixture generally leaves the one-parameter exponential family, so a single count is no longer sufficient
Because exponential families forbid extra variance
Because T(y) is undefined for counts
check.answer: To mark that a finite mixture generally leaves the one-parameter exponential family, so a single count is no longer sufficient
check.why: The plate is a workshop map, including the exit door. Heteroresistance mixtures are the TB-shaped version of that exit.
